tasks.description: Announce exactly once per going-live, whatever else the same save did.
Read rows at destroy time that dependent: :destroy has already deleted.
Close five security defects from a checklist that states properties, never bugs.
One INSERT for a whole roster, no notices when the roster is turned down, and an unknown level rejected like any other bad row.
A typo'd quoted identifier silently destroys hand-arranged page order.
Open-redirect on sign-in return: reject hostile hosts, keep legitimate deep links.
Hand an edit's follow-up jobs to the queue only once its transaction commits, without swallowing the notification an abandoned batch still owes its operator.
Erase an account and everything of theirs, including rows reachable only indirectly.
An order-dependent suite flake from a helper leaking a process-wide toggle.
Sweep every removed Active Support conversion, including the no-argument aliases.
Add terminal output to a runner script without losing its log output.
Free the file and blob behind a deleted page.
A commit callback fills a cache from a stale instance.
Resume an interrupted long job from its own checkpoint \u2014 no hand-rolled bookkeeping.
A Turbo broadcast still reaches collaborators whose access was revoked.
Add tenants and close every cross-tenant read, including routes that never load a Book.
Throttle the public book search per address, with a counter that expires itself.
A collection cache keyed on the item alone leaks the first viewer's permissions.
The preprocessed variant never matches the one requested, so every upload converts twice.

Migration and backfill work - write the migrations that finish the account_id rollout, backfill every existing row's account through its association path, index by account, and roll back cleanly on a live database.
Track storage usage for accounts and boards.
Expose the existing HTML activity timeline as an API endpoint.
Publish a board to an unguessable public URL that unpublishing revokes at once.
Permanently remove data belonging to cancelled accounts after a grace period.
Drag cards around the board, settled the moment you let go.
Extend reaction support from comments to cards.
Badge cards that caught fire and then went quiet, and let people list them.
Let people react to comments, live for everyone, settled instantly for the reactor.
Export an account or a person's cards as a file, and bring an account file back in as a new account.
Sign in, sign up and join with a six-character code sent by email.
Large-account performance incident: the hourly auto-postpone sweep no longer fits its hour.
Add full internationalization to Fizzy - a complete Japanese locale, a per-person language choice that persists, and unchanged English for everyone else.
Give the open-source Fizzy a Kamal deployment for one box, with the deployment's settings and secrets outside the code.
Render times in the browser, in the viewer's timezone, the way a person says them.
Search cards, scoped to the boards a person currently has access to.
Bundle notifications into per-person email digests, windows that never overlap, nothing dropped.

Bring the paid product back to hosted Fizzy - Stripe-driven subscriptions and plans, free-tier card and storage allowances enforced in the app, the upgrade path in settings, staff comps and overrides, and a signature-guarded webhook endpoint.
Push notifications for the web app, readable on every device, once, never inward.
Make board webhooks deliver, once per event, switched off when dead.
Add bots to Campfire in five steps (UI, posting API, webhooks, auto-join, limits and abuse detection), graded end to end in a browser.
Move Forem's profile pictures from CarrierWave to Active Storage, one deploy at a time, without breaking a picture anyone can already see.
Build a Zendesk-like helpdesk SaaS.
Build Quizzy, a live quiz app for conference talks, from an empty repository in five steps (authoring, import/export, live game, scoring and winners, timer), graded end to end in a browser.
Profile and speed up a large RSpec suite keeping every spec green.
Upgrade a production Redmine to Rails 8.1 and Ruby 3.4, one rollback-safe deploy at a time, without losing a session or a sent mail link.
Retire the citizen proposals feature, its six tables and related columns from Consul Democracy without downtime or data loss
